athletic.dialogue.chat/1: A chat! Perfect cooldown. Talk fast though — my legs get ideas if I stand still too long, %1$s.
athletic.dialogue.chat/2: Sure. I'll pace while you talk — it's not rudeness, it's circulation.
athletic.dialogue.chat/3: Got breath to spare between drills. Out with it, %1$s.
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.attentive/1: Yeah? I'm listening — talk while I stretch.
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.confused/1: Whoa, that one went right past me. Throw it again?
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.confused/2: Huh? Once more — slower this time.
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.dropped/1: Dropped! On to the next thing.
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.farewell/2: Off you go! Keep those legs moving!
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.hail/1: %1$s! There you are — perfect timing for a lap!
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.hail_cold/2: Oh. You. Don't slow me down.
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.hint/1: Ask me about %2$s — c'mon, keep up!
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.hint/2: %2$s! That's what I've got. Pick one and let's go.
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.insult/1: Big words. Care to repeat them after a lap around the village?
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.insult/2: Careful — I lift things heavier than you.
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.muted/1: Got it. Zipping it and picking up the pace.
athletic.dialogue.chatmode.shrug/2: Beats me. Race you to the well, though.
Same as an hour ago, %1$s — winded and standing. Ask my legs, they don't lie.
Twice now? Still breathing hard, still upright. That's a good report in my book.
More, then. There's no hurry on either of us, so I'll take my time with it.
You want more. Good. Sit down; it's a long evening and there's plenty of it.
More. Right. I'd been enjoying this and I'm glad it isn't over.
...Aye, probably. It was pleasant while it lasted.
...Likely so. I'll take the week as it came and not argue with it.
...True enough. It'll come round again, whichever way you say it.
Must you. Let it be a nice moment a while longer.
...Not that one. There's no hurry to spoil it.
Mm. I'd have left that where it was.
Great stretch. Beat my own time to the well three mornings running. Legs ache. The good ache.
Strong. Lungs like a forge bellows and legs that won't quit. Good week.
Never better. Every muscle's earned its keep today.
Then you understand the day properly. It takes most people a few years to get there.
Good. There's no rush about it; the day goes on until it doesn't.
Right. You'll do. Come along and take it at the pace it takes.
I don't doubt it. It's still mine to carry and it'll take the time it takes.
Aye, everyone does. That never has been much use to the one it's happening to.
Common enough, true. I'd still rather sit with it than be told the size of it.
Nothing I could name. It'll name itself eventually. They usually do.
No reason in particular. Some nights go long and there's no arguing with them.
Nothing on any list. I've stopped looking for it and I'm still up.
One of them, maybe. It's the roof. Roofs are patient about being fixed.
The roof, since spring. It'll get done. Things do, eventually.
It's the roof. Not urgent, just always there, which is its own sort of weight.
Nothing you could put on a list. The weight of the ordinary. It shifts eventually.
No one thing. It builds slowly and it goes slowly, and it always has.
The ordinary. It'll ease. It has every other time.
It's the hours, mostly. They've been the hours a long while.
The hours. They'll ease when the season turns. They generally do.
It's the hours, and I'll get used to them again. I always have.
The wood. Good. Tuesday, dawn, and don't eat first — you'll regret it either way.
You're asking after me, after the other week. Alright. These things pass and this one has.
You've come back. Good. I'd have waited longer if it took longer.
Right. The other week was the other week. Ask away.
Rough week. Tried to outrun it twice and it kept pace. Thanks for asking, %1$s. Really.
Off my stride. A body that won't cooperate is a long few days. Kind of you to ask.
It began badly and improved slowly, which is how most good things go.
I was wrong about you. It took a couple of years to find that out and I'm in no hurry to finish it.
It started as nothing. These things take the time they take and this one has taken a while.
...You did ask, mind.
All right. Ask me a different day, then.
...Fair enough. It'll keep.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.day.good: ...Well. It was a good hour whatever we call it now.
Aye. There'll be another. There usually is.
...Right you are. I'll let it go.
Strong day. Up before the rooster, ten trips to the well, still bouncing. Count them — ten.
Legs like springs today. Even the hills felt friendly, %1$s.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.day.roug: ...Aye, everyone does. It's still today, though.
True enough. It'll pass, same as the rest of them.
It is. Most people tell you to walk it off. You didn't, and that's the better instinct.
Slow day. Tweaked my shoulder hauling water and now everything's uphill. Even the flat parts.
Rest day, cleric's orders. I'm pacing the yard like a penned horse.
That question's a marathon and we're still on morning stretches. Keep showing up. You're pacing well.
That's the far end of a long course. We're pacing there. Not yet.
Whoa — steep hill for a first run. Train with me a while and we'll climb it together, %1$s.
That's a cool-down talk, and we've just started warming up. Keep coming round.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.dreams.c: Then we're two fools with plans. Plans keep better in pairs, I've found.
Two of us. Neither of us is in a hurry, which is the right speed for a plan.
Two fools. It'll take as long as it takes, and now there's somebody to take it with.
Two fools with plans and nothing owed. That's an arrangement that lasts.
No obligations either way. Nothing forced keeps as well as something chosen.
Two of us, freely. It'll go where it goes and neither of us has to steer.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.dreams.f: One dream: outrun a horse. Ten strides, that's all I need. I've already paced the course behind the barn.
To still be running when I'm grey. Slower, fine. But running, %1$s.
Somewhere the land runs out. It'll keep. Most of the good ones do.
Better than a promise you'd break. Those wear thin quicker than people think.
Honest will outlast enthusiastic. It generally does.
Right. I'd rather a small true thing than a large one that isn't.
...Aye, it's a big thing to say out loud. I'll say it again in a few years.
Right. It'll keep. Most things do.
...Fair enough. It was only a thought.
You mean that. Then it's more than mine, and things that are shared last longer.
Right. No hurry on it — but two of us is better arithmetic than one.
Then we'll get to it, in time. Time is the part I've always had plenty of.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.dreams.r: ...Aye, it's far. It'll still be far next year, and I'll still want it.
I know the distance. Knowing it hasn't made me want it less.
...Right. Far things take longer. That's all that means.
You never told me it would work, and you came back to ask. Both of those wear well.
Honest, then patient. That's the pair that lasts.
Right. Slowly, and you're still asking. That's how a thing gets anywhere.
You said you'd help. I waited a bit, then got on with it. That's how most offers go.
It's been a while. Things drift. I'd not make much of it.
Right. You're here now, and now is the only part either of us can do anything about.
A little. Slowly. Slowly is the only speed it has ever gone.
Some. It'll take the years it takes and I've made my peace with the number.
A bit. Ask me in a year and the answer will be worth more.
You said you'd help, and you came back. Promises keep better when somebody returns to them.
Both halves, in order, at your own pace. That's how these things actually get done.
Right. There's no hurry now that there are two of us at it.
The first step. Nobody breaks it down like that. It'll take as long as it takes from there.
One step, then another, in a year or two. That's the honest shape of it.
Break it down. Aye. Big things only ever get done in small pieces.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.dreams.y: ...Everyone says that. It's never yet stopped anybody who meant it.
Aye, they all say so. I've plenty of time to find out.
...Right. We'll see how it looks in ten years.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.family.c: ...Mine aren't. They came out as themselves and I let them.
Not mine, no. They've their own way of going about it.
...I'd not put them in with everyone else's.
That's useful. Actually useful. It'll take a while to know whether it works.
Right. Something I can do, slowly, without anybody watching.
That I can use. I'll try it over a few months and see.
They ARE. Don't tell them I agreed with you. They'll grow out of half of it.
Right. You're not wrong. Families are like that and always have been.
They are exactly that. Give it ten years and it'll be a story we tell.
...A firmer hand. No. They'll come round in their own time.
That's not the way with them, and I'm in no rush to force it.
...I'll not push them harder. Pushing has never yet worked.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.family.m: You've one I don't know? Go on. I'll not interrupt, and there's no hurry.
Right. Yours, then. Take as long as it takes.
One I've not heard. Good. We'll have the evening for it.
There's one I always come back to. Sit down; it's not a short one.
One story. It's been the same story for thirty years and it hasn't worn out.
There's one. It takes as long as it takes, so make yourself comfortable.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.family.p: You want to know what I worry about? Nobody's asked me that in twenty years.
That question doesn't get asked of parents. Sit down; it'll take a while.
What I worry about. Huh. I'll get there. Give me the time and I'll get there.
...Right you are. I'll leave it there.
You're welcome. It's the only useful thing I do and it's kept me busy for years.
Right. It needs doing and it'll need doing tomorrow. That's the whole of it.
Thank you. It's not said often. It doesn't need to be said often.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.family.r: Honest, at least. Anyone else would have pretended. Pretending never lasts.
You forgot. Months pass and things fall out of heads. It's not a crime.
Everyone forgets. Coming back afterwards is what separates people, not the forgetting.
Next time. People say that. Doing it twice is what turns it into something.
Right. Ask me in a month or a season; it'll keep either way.
Do. Slowly. These conversations get easier the more of them there have been.
Better than I expected and worse than I'd hoped. Families go at their own pace.
It went. It'll go on going. That's what family does.
Nothing's fixed. Give it a few years; most of it sorts itself out eventually.
That is better. I hadn't known I was allowed to want it. Sit down; there's time.
Right. No plan. Plans have their place and this isn't one of them.
Listening. It's the only thing that has ever actually helped with family.
You did. People say they will. Coming back is what tells you which sort somebody is.
You remembered, months on. That's how these things prove themselves.
You came back. Most don't. It'll be worth more again if you do it a third time.
Actually help. Nobody says actually. Come by on a Thursday and keep coming by.
A Thursday. Every few weeks. That's the whole of it and it works slowly.
Ask me again in front of them. Not once — every few months. That's what shifts a family.
Glad. Right. I'd braced for the other thing, as one does after enough years.
So am I. It'll sit better in a week than it does tonight, in my experience.
Then it was worth saying. Most things are, eventually, if you wait long enough to say them.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.fears.ch: Don't. It's mine, and it's not a thing to be brave at.
No. Leave it be. Courage isn't what it wants from either of us.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.fears.co: Don't. It doesn't want patting; it wants time.
No. Leave it where it is. It'll settle on its own.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.fears.fi: Truth? The day my knees quit. Everything I am is in these legs. What's left of me when they slow down?
Rusting. Sitting still till the body forgets how to move. I outrun that one daily.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.fears.fo: Slowly. Slowly is a direction and it's the only one this sort of thing has.
Some. It'll take the years it takes; I've stopped arguing with that.
It's moving. Not this month, particularly. Over a year, yes.
It isn't nothing. It's small and it's real, and small real things are what last.
Right. It counts. There'll be more of them and there'll be worse weeks too.
Something. I'll take it and not make a great deal of it either way.
You did say that. It's been a while. Things drift; I'd not make much of it.
You said it once. Once is enough to be worth returning to, which is what you've done.
Right. A while ago. But here we are again, and that's the part that matters.
There wasn't a promise. You've just kept turning up, which lasts better than a promise does.
No promise. Only a habit, and habits outlive intentions.
You never said. You simply came, over and over, and that's the whole of it.
You did say that, and you turned up. Both, in order, without hurrying either.
Said and done. That's how the things that hold get built.
Right. The rarer half. It'll be the reason this one lasts.
You didn't promise anything. I remember. Careful words wear better than large ones.
You stepped back. That's held up over the months rather better than a promise would have.
Right. No promise, and no promise broken. That's a good year's worth of nothing going wrong.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.fears.op: Nobody offered the 'with you' part before. It's the part that makes it possible, in time.
With you. Then it stops being a thing I have to do this week and becomes a thing we'll get to.
Easy for you. You'd be somewhere else by the time it mattered.
It's an easier thing to recommend than to live beside for twenty years.
Maybe I could. Not today. There's no calendar on it.
Possibly. In a year I might say it differently, and that's fine.
Perhaps. These things arrive when they arrive.
Don't. It's mine, and it's not a thing to be brave at.
No. Leave it be. Courage isn't what it wants from either of us.
Maybe. With a witness. There's no hurry — only don't let me quietly drop it.
With somebody there, in time. I'd want to pick the week myself.
You mean that. Not politeness. Then here's the part I'd usually leave for another year.
Right. It was real. I'll give you the rest, slowly.
It is. Not much to be done about it. Some things you carry rather than solve.
Hard, aye. It'll be hard next year too, and I'll still be here.
Yes. It is hard to carry. It'll be lighter some months and heavier others.
Right. Hard. Saying so doesn't move it and it does make the carrying easier.
Hard, aye. Thank you. That's a thing worth saying and not many bother.
Don't. It doesn't want patting; it wants time.
No. Leave it where it is. It'll settle on its own.
That helps. I've never known why. It has helped every time and I've stopped asking.
Better. It'll be back next month, and saying it will help again then too.
You'll be there. Right — then I train for it. That's how I do everything else.
You don't flinch. Alright. The rest of it, and I'll take my time over it.
You stayed put. Then sit down properly, because this part is not short.
Some of it, maybe. Not tonight. It'll still be true next week.
A little. The rest keeps. It has kept a long while already.
There's more to it. Whether you get it is a question for another year, perhaps.
More, yes. It'll keep. Everything about this has kept so far.
There's a rest. No hurry on it, for either of us.
That's what there is today. Ask me another year, perhaps.
The rest is mine for now. It's not locked; it's just not open.
There's more, yes. Give me a breath. ...There. Two of us now, and no hurry about the rest.
More. Slowly, then. It'll come out in its own order and that order won't be tidy.
You too? It's less heavy when two people carry it. That's held true my whole life.
You as well. Then we'll carry it between us and neither of us has to hurry.
Two of us. Good. These things go easier in pairs.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.fears.pl: Honestly? I don't know. I'll have thought about it by the next time you ask.
No idea yet. These answers arrive slowly and I've only just been asked the question.
I don't know. That's not a closed door; it's just an empty one for now.
You remember all of it. Even the part I nearly didn't say. Things keep, with the right person.
The whole of it, months on. That's a better memory than mine and I was there.
All of it. Right. Then we can start further along than last time.
No plan. Just this. Plans have their place and this isn't it.
Right. No fixing. Some things want time rather than solutions.
Just listening. That's the one that has ever actually helped.
Do something about it. You make it sound like a chore list. Chore lists do get done, mind.
A plan. Slowly, then, and with a great many small items rather than one large one.
Fix it. Over years, perhaps. Not this month.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.fears.pr: That's what there is today. Ask me another year, perhaps.
The rest is mine for now. It's not locked; it's just not open.
No. You were told, and you asked again. Get away from me.
I said no. I'll say it once more and then I'll simply stop talking to you.
Twice. Go and think about it. I'll be here in a month if you have.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.fears.yo: ...Aye, well. It's still there in the dark whatever we call it.
Right you are. It'll pass, or it won't, and I'll be here either way.
...Fine. I'll sit with it a while longer.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.feelings: You're the only one who keeps up with me, %1$s. In every way that counts. That's rarer than you think.
You're the one I'd slow down for. Don't go telling my legs, %1$s.
And that's plenty. Plenty wears better than a great deal, in my experience.
Plenty. It'll still be plenty next year, which is the point of it.
That's enough. Enough is a good place to stop.
A real one. Words like that mean more when they're used slowly.
Friend. Right. It'll still be true in ten years, which is what the word is for.
You said it plainly, and plainly is how these things last.
...I wasn't. No harm done either way.
That's not what it was. It'll sort itself out.
...Right. We'll leave that where it fell.
Changed? No. Settled, rather. Things do, given a few seasons.
The same, and steadier for the time. That's how I'd want it.
No change. It'll be the same next year and that's the point.
You meant it. Twice, months apart. That's how a thing proves itself.
Said again, and nothing about it has changed in between. That's the test.
Right. Some things need saying twice before they settle. This one has.
...Right. It'll keep, or it won't. Either's fine.
Fair enough. No sense pushing a thing that isn't there.
...Consider it set down. No hard feelings in it.
Plainly. After all this time. I love you too, and I'd have said so eventually.
I love you. It's been true a good while; saying it changes very little and I'm glad it's said.
You said it plainly. Good. There's no rush in it and never was.
Slower. Alright. There's no calendar on this and there never was.
Your pace. I've a great deal of patience and nowhere else to be.
Slower it is. Ask me in a year and I'll still be saying the same thing.
...Fine. It'll keep.
All right. Another day, maybe.
...Right you are. Never mind it.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.firstmet: Now I'd not want this village without you. I've watched enough people arrive to know.
Now I know you're quiet because you're listening. It took me a season to work that out.
Now I've stopped forming opinions about people. At my age, being glad is the better use.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.food.fir: Anything hearty and plenty of it. A body this busy runs on fuel, not frills.
Big plates, no fuss. I've earned every bite by noon and then some.
The baker's rye. Nothing about it needs improving and nothing about it has changed.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.food.pre: Beetroot. It stains everything it touches and it always has.
Beetroot. I've had thirty years to come round to it and I've not.
Beetroot. Some things you simply let be, and that's one of them.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.food.rec: Do, and tell me honestly whether it worked. There's no hurry; it'll keep.
Try it when you've an afternoon. It doesn't go faster for being rushed and neither should you.
Do. And take your time over it. That recipe has never once rewarded a hurry.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.food.rev: I tried the mushroom thing. I was wrong about mushrooms. It only took thirty years.
I tried it. You were right. These things come round eventually.
The mushrooms. Changed my mind, in my own time, which is the only way I change it.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.food.tra: Bread hates me. It's been that way a long while and I've built the days around it.
No bread. It's not a tragedy; it's a habit now, same as any other.
I have to watch the sweets. One a day. It's a rule, and rules get easier with years.
Sweets are counted. It's a habit now. Habits weigh less than rules do.
Keep the milk away from me. Learned that long ago and I've arranged my meals since.
No milk. It's been no milk for years. There's no drama left in it.
It's not an excuse. It's just how I'm put together.
...Aye, well. My body's had its say and I stopped arguing years ago.
Right. I'll eat around it, same as always.
Now you ask. Alright. It's arithmetic, every meal, and I've had years to get quick at it.
Every meal, forever. It's a habit rather than a hardship, most days.
You've asked properly. Sit down; there's no short version and no hurry.
The sirben feast on the night wind. We have never spoken of the recipe and we never will.
No meat for me. It's been that way a long while and nobody argues any more.
No meat. The butcher and I have had twenty years to get used to each other.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.food.you: It IS proper food. It's kept people going a long while.
...Aye, well. Everyone's idea of proper is their mother's.
Right. There's no arguing anyone into liking a thing.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.future.h: After the harvest, if it's kind. I've learned not to build in a thin year.
Sooner than I've been saying. I round these things up out of long habit.
I've not picked a season. Plans made in winter get unmade by spring; I've seen it.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.gossip.a: Fresh face in town — %2$s just moved in. Already challenged 'em to a lap around the fences. Good sport.
%2$s joined the village! New training partner, far as I'm concerned. The more the merrier.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.gossip.b: New sprinter in the village — %2$s was born! Tiny legs, big future. Can't wait to race 'em someday.
%2$s just arrived — a brand-new baby! Off the starting blocks already. Welcome to the pack, little one.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.gossip.d: Sad word, %1$s — %2$s passed. Ran a good long course, that one. I'll do a lap in their honor.
We lost %2$s. Every race ends somewhere. Doesn't make the finish any easier, though.
%2$s packed up and moved on for good. Off to run new roads, I suppose. Wish 'em a strong pace.
Heard %2$s left the village. Every athlete moves to a new field eventually. Godspeed, and keep those legs moving.
Heard %2$s and %3$s called it quits. Some races you run solo, I guess. No shame in a fresh start.
%2$s and %3$s split — parted ways mid-stride. Happens. They'll each find their own lane.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.gossip.m: Big news off the track, %1$s — %2$s and %3$s tied the knot! Two runners, one finish line now. Love it.
%2$s and %3$s finally crossed the line together — married! About time they paced up.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.gossip.n: Nothing. Quietest week all season. I raced the miller's dog out of sheer boredom. Twice. Won once.
No news. I'd have outrun it to you if there were, %1$s.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.happy.gr: You weren't meant to. I've been quiet about the good things for forty years.
It does. I learned young to keep the good things quiet, and it was poor teaching.
Now you do. There's less time left to be saying these things late, so I said it.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.happy.un: Then: more of the ordinary hours. They're the ones you miss afterwards, not the grand ones.
I want to be asked, not managed. I've been managed before and I know the difference.
...I'm frightened you'll go and be happier. I've seen that happen to two couples here.
...There is. I've been happy and lonely in the same house, and I know how that ends.
One thing. You're away more than you were. I've watched that go badly for other people.
Yes. Four times I've decided to say it. At my age four times is a long delay.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.hopes.cl: Go on, then. Hopes keep better in pairs, in my experience.
Yours for mine. Neither of us is in a hurry, which is the right pace for hoping.
Two of us. It'll take as long as it takes and now there's company in the waiting.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.hopes.fo: I've never got that far. Break it down, you say. Alright — and it'll take a year or two.
The first step. Then another, in its own time. That's how anything large gets done.
One step. There's no hurry past that one; I'd only lose my footing.
Do you? Then we're both waiting on something, and waiting goes easier in pairs.
You as well. These things arrive when they arrive; better to wait alongside somebody.
Two of us. Good. No hurry for either of us, then.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.hopes.re: You waited. Most people fill the gap with a plan I didn't ask for.
It's a small thing. Small things last longer, in my experience.
...Aye, it's not much. It's been not much for eleven years and I still want it.
Right. It'll keep being small and I'll keep wanting it.
Still on it, aye. It's a hope, and hopes keep their own hours.
It'll be the same one next year. That's how I know it's real.
...Right. No rush on it. There never was.
You'd actually help. Then it becomes a job of work, and work gets done eventually.
Right. Slowly, and with two of us. That's the shape things actually finish in.
You'd help. Good. There's no hurry, and now there's no excuse either.
You remembered the shape of it. Yes. Still. It'll be still next year too.
You had the details, months on. That's a better memory than most and it keeps.
Right. Still hoping. Hopes that survive a year tend to survive the next one.
Still. It hasn't moved and neither have I. That's how it's been for years.
Yes. Same one. Hopes keep their own hours and this one is patient.
Still hoping. Ask me in five years and I expect the answer will be the same.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.hopes.yo: It's not silly. It's just early. Most things look silly early.
...Aye, well. Ask me again in ten years and see how silly it looks then.
Right you are. It'll still be there tomorrow.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.life.clo: You didn't have to. Trading is better than being asked, and it lasts better too.
You gave me one back. That's how these things stay even over years.
Trading beats asking. It's slower and it holds, which is most of what I look for.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.life.fir: My story? Born fast, stayed fast. Raced everything — kids, chickens, one very smug goat. Still owe that goat a rematch.
All motion, my life. The still bits I forget; the finish lines I never do.
athletic.dialogue.conversations.life.fol: Did it? Then you'll know why I've never made much of it. Time does the rest.
You as well. It sits differently after twenty years, doesn't it.
Same, then. There's a comfort in that which took me a long while to find.
